overview.title: Mazagan as a whole
overview.p1: The Portuguese City — still often called Mazagan — is the fortified heart of El Jadida and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Ramparts, gates, the cistern and the dense streets inside form one ensemble.
overview.p2: Treat it as a walkable district rather than a single monument. Start at the cistern, climb to the Bastion of the Angel, then lose an hour in the lanes.
overview.p3: This is Atlantic fortress heritage, not inland medina fantasy: stone, wind and sea define the mood.

q1.question: Is the whole city UNESCO listed?
q1.answer: The Portuguese City (Mazagan) is the listed fortified ensemble.

q2.question: One ticket for everything?
q2.answer: The cistern has its own ticket; wall walks are generally open.

q3.question: How long for a first visit?
q3.answer: Half a day covers the highlights without rushing.

q4.question: Guided tour useful?
q4.answer: Yes if you want military and trade history in detail.

q5.question: Best photo spots?
q5.answer: Cistern interior and the Bastion of the Angel toward the ocean.
